need: The business must deliver ultra-fast (under 60 minutes) access to fresh perishables and daily essentials to customers who prioritize speed and convenience over cost.
why: This fulfills the core customer need for immediate gratification and reduces the friction of traditional grocery shopping, driving repeat usage and high ratings.

need: The business must provide a unified digital interface that aggregates fragmented inventory from multiple store partners to offer a comprehensive assortment without requiring customers to visit multiple locations.
why: This creates value by simplifying the shopping experience and enabling the platform to monetize through transaction commissions and advertising on a consolidated marketplace.

need: The business must optimize last-mile logistics through algorithmic routing and a dense network of gig workers to ensure efficient order fulfillment and cost control.
why: This operational efficiency is critical for maintaining profitability in a low-margin model while meeting the strict time commitments required to satisfy the 'quick commerce' promise.

need: The business needs to measure and report on the percentage of orders fulfilled within the target timeframe (e.g., <60 minutes) to validate operational efficiency and service speed commitments.
why: Meeting strict delivery windows is the core value proposition of the Q-Commerce model and directly drives customer retention and repeat usage.

need: The business needs to track the rate of inventory discrepancies and overselling incidents to ensure accurate availability data and minimize order failures.
why: Accurate inventory synchronization is critical for maintaining customer trust and preventing revenue loss from failed deliveries in a high-velocity environment.

need: The business needs to monitor the efficiency of revenue streams, specifically the ratio of transaction commissions and delivery fees against operational costs, to ensure profitability.
why: Sustaining the gig-economy logistics model requires rigorous cost control and optimization of multiple monetization channels to achieve a positive unit economics.

need: The business needs to provide a transparent, real-time dashboard for Store Partners to view their specific order volume, revenue splits, and performance metrics against the platform's overall goals.
why: Store Partners require visibility into their contribution to the platform's success and their individual financial performance to optimize staffing and inventory, which is not explicitly covered by existing agreement or quality management requirements.

need: The business needs to enable Delivery Partners to access historical earnings summaries, payout schedules, and tax documents directly within the platform interface.
why: Gig-economy workers need immediate access to their financial history and compliance documents to manage their personal finances and tax obligations, a need distinct from the platform's internal settlement and audit logging functions.

need: The business needs to offer a dedicated customer-facing portal for managing subscription preferences, viewing detailed delivery history, and accessing personalized loyalty rewards beyond simple point accrual.
why: Customers require a centralized hub to manage their recurring commitments and view the full value of their loyalty status, which goes beyond the basic feedback collection and profile management currently defined.

need: The business needs to implement a robust dynamic pricing engine that adjusts delivery fees and commissions based on real-time demand, weather, and traffic conditions.
why: Static pricing models fail in hyperlocal Q-Commerce where supply and demand fluctuate rapidly, directly impacting revenue optimization and SLA adherence.

need: The business needs to implement automated, real-time inventory reconciliation between physical store POS systems and the digital platform to prevent overselling and revenue leakage.
why: In a hyperlocal model where speed is critical, discrepancies between physical stock and digital availability lead to failed deliveries, customer dissatisfaction, and financial loss from uncollectible orders.

need: The business needs to continuously monitor and mitigate financial risks such as fraud, chargebacks, and payment provider failures to protect cash flow and ensure settlement reliability.
why: In a high-volume, low-margin transaction model, even small percentages of failed settlements or fraudulent activity can significantly impact net revenue and operational sustainability.

need: The business must secure regulatory compliance regarding food safety standards and labor laws for gig-economy workers before launch.
why: Operating without adherence to these external regulations creates immediate legal liability and operational risk that cannot be mitigated post-launch.

need: The business needs to deploy predictive risk analytics that correlate delivery delays, inventory errors, and customer sentiment to proactively identify and mitigate threats to brand reputation and SLA performance.
why: In a low-margin, high-volume Q-commerce environment, reactive measures are too slow to protect brand equity; proactive identification of operational friction points is essential to maintain customer trust and retention.

need: The business must dynamically calculate and collect applicable taxes based on local jurisdiction rules, as tax compliance is a mandatory financial settlement requirement.
why: Failure to accurately apply varying tax rates across different service areas violates financial regulations and exposes the platform to penalties.

need: The business must validate regulatory compliance and contractual terms for all Store Partners and Delivery Partners before onboarding, as operational readiness depends on these external validations.
why: Operating with unverified partners violates labor and safety policies, creating liability and disrupting the supply chain.

need: The business must guarantee the rapid isolation and containment of system outages or data corruption to prevent the propagation of errors across the entire order lifecycle and protect revenue integrity.
why: In a hyperlocal model where speed is the primary value proposition, any system failure directly translates to missed delivery windows, customer churn, and potential regulatory breaches if food safety or labor laws are violated due to lack of oversight.

need: The business must guarantee the immediate and transparent resolution of financial disputes and fraud attempts to maintain trust with both Store Partners and Customers while minimizing revenue leakage.
why: Given the high volume of micro-transactions and reliance on third-party settlement, the inability to quickly reverse fraudulent charges or resolve billing disputes would erode partner confidence and trigger regulatory scrutiny regarding fund handling.

need: The business must guarantee the preservation of an immutable audit trail for all operational anomalies to satisfy regulatory authorities and facilitate root cause analysis during high-stakes investigations.
why: With significant regulatory exposure regarding gig-worker labor laws and food safety, the business cannot rely on verbal explanations; a verifiable, tamper-proof record of who did what and when is required to mitigate legal liability and prove compliance.

need: The business needs to dynamically scale its micro-fulfillment network and partner onboarding processes to maintain ultra-fast delivery SLAs as it expands into new geographic zones.
why: Growth in locations and partners introduces complexity that, if not managed, will degrade the core value proposition of speed and reliability, leading to customer churn.

need: The business needs to implement scalable, automated quality assurance and dispute resolution workflows to handle increased order volume without compromising service standards.
why: As volume and offerings grow, manual oversight becomes a bottleneck; automated quality control is essential to protect brand reputation and ensure consistent customer satisfaction.

need: The business needs to establish flexible, data-driven revenue management and settlement mechanisms that adapt to diverse partner types and dynamic market conditions.
why: Scaling the partner ecosystem requires a monetization model that can efficiently handle varying commission structures, multi-currency transactions, and real-time reconciliation to sustain profitability.

need: The business needs to produce predictive analytics reports on demand patterns and inventory turnover to optimize resource allocation and reduce overselling incidents.
why: In a model dependent on real-time inventory synchronization and ultra-fast delivery, forward-looking insights are critical for balancing supply with fluctuating demand and minimizing operational waste.

need: The business needs to implement automated fallback routing and vendor diversification strategies to maintain order fulfillment when external logistics providers or mapping services experience outages.
why: Third-party logistics and mapping dependencies are single points of failure that can halt the ultra-fast delivery promise, directly impacting customer satisfaction and revenue.

need: The business needs to secure Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with critical third-party vendors that include guaranteed uptime, rapid incident response, and financial penalties for service degradation.
why: Without contractual protections and performance guarantees, the business is exposed to operational downtime and reputational damage from vendor failures that are outside its direct control.

need: The business can safely defer the implementation of advanced predictive inventory replenishment and complex demand forecasting models until after initial market data is collected.
why: These features rely on historical transaction patterns and traffic data that only become available after the service has been live and processing orders.

need: The business needs to minimize waste and maintain product quality by proactively managing perishable stock before it becomes unsellable.
why: The system shall generate real-time alerts for inventory items approaching their shelf-life limits to prioritize fulfillment or trigger removal.

need: The business needs to ensure customers receive timely, consistent updates across all preferred channels to reduce support inquiries and improve the delivery experience.
why: The system shall orchestrate multi-channel notifications (SMS, email, app push) by automatically triggering messages when an Order Request status changes to Ready for Delivery or Assigned to a Delivery Partner.
